method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase of complement closure theorem and corollary, with formula, macro, label and reference parity after bounded index projections. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: A set is computable exactly when it and its complement are c.e.; non-c.e. complement of the halting set K_0.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: C.e. sets are not closed under complement. The theorem says that for any set A of naturals, A is computable if and only if both A and its complement in the naturals are c.e.
samples.checks: The quantification, complement expression, two-way condition and distinction between computable and c.e. are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If A is computable, its complement is computable by the characteristic-function identity, hence both are c.e. Conversely, choose d with domain A and e with domain its complement. The µ-search h finds a halting witness for one branch, so h is total. Membership in A is exactly T(d,x,h(x)), a computable test. The frozen source mistakenly used e in that final test, which would decide complement membership.
samples.checks: The characteristic identity, d/e domain assignment, disjunction, totality and corrected A test agree. OLCMP-020 documents the two exact formula corrections and associated index prose.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The informal procedure searches in parallel for halting of φ_d or φ_e. One halts because A and its complement partition the naturals. Halting of φ_d signifies A, and halting of φ_e signifies its complement.
samples.checks: The frozen e/f pair includes an unbound f and reverses the A assignment; the Marathi explanation uses the previously defined d/e pair consistently.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The complement of K_0 is not c.e.: K_0 itself is c.e. but noncomputable, so c.e. of its complement would make K_0 computable by the theorem, contradicting the earlier result.
samples.checks: The complement, contradiction, theorem label and K_0 reference with its option are preserved.

source_observations: T068 supplies पूरक संच, T198 supplies अनुप्रमेय and T327 distinguishes c.e. from ordinary countability.
OLCMP-020 records wrong e and unbound f indices in the frozen formal/informal arguments. The Marathi correction is projected back only for mechanical parity comparison.
